samples.summary: Flipping the affinity-less START default from backward to forward changes geometry for every `computeSelectionRects` consumer, not just user selections, and deviates from the issue's stated "keep the backward default".
samples.evidence: `buildRects` now does `const startAffinity = start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward'`. `computeSelectionRects` is not selection-only: it is also used for find-match rects and scroll-into-view (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3129-3135), spell-check squiggles (docs/design/docs/docs-spell-check.md:162 says squiggles reuse `computeSelectionRects(...)`), comment/peer highlights (editor.ts:1620, 1640, 1659, 1676) and peer selections published by older clients that never send `lineAffinity`. None of those callers attach an affinity, so all of them silently change which visual line the first rect lands on at a wrap boundary. The task file itself records this as a deliberate deviation from the issue wording (docs/tasks/active/20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md:18-26, 63-67), but the deviation is only justified for user selections; the non-selection consumers of the shared helper are not analysed anywhere in the change or in the updated design docs (docs/design/docs/docs-local-caret-anchoring.md:83-87 describes it purely as selection behavior). A narrower fit would have been to default only when the endpoint came from a hit test, or to pass the default in at the selection call site.

samples.summary: Caret affinity now lives in two places (`Cursor.lineAffinity` and `DocPosition.lineAffinity`) with no synchronisation, so the anchoring round-trip the change claims to fix only works for click-derived carets.
samples.evidence: `Cursor.moveTo(pos, affinity)` stores `this.position = pos` and `this.lineAffinity = affinity` independently (cursor.ts:28-32). After this change some call sites put the affinity on the position too (text-editor.ts:1521-1525, editor.ts restoreLocalCursor) while the keyboard paths do not: `handleHome` calls `this.cursor.moveTo(newPos, 'forward')` with `newPos` carrying no `lineAffinity` (text-editor.ts:2818), and `moveHorizontal`/vertical do the same at text-editor.ts:2780/2795 (the movers at text-editor.ts:3887-3999 build fresh `{blockId, offset}` objects). Since presence/anchoring is fed from `cursor.position` (docs-view.tsx:394-399 -> `updateCursorPos`), a caret placed by Home or arrow-right publishes no affinity and `restoreLocalCursor` re-collapses it onto the previous visual line — exactly the failure the new comment in editor.ts says it is preventing. The redundancy is visible in the diff itself, where `restoreLocalCursor` has to pass the same value twice (in the position object and as the `moveTo` argument). A single source of truth (moveTo writing the affinity onto the stored position, or the cursor keeping only the field) is the fitting design.

samples.summary: Table-cell selection endpoints never get a `lineAffinity`, so the cell-internal plumbing added to `buildRects` is unreachable and the reported wrap-boundary bug persists inside cells.
samples.evidence: The diff threads `startAffinity`/`endAffinity` into the cell-internal branch (`resolvePositionPixel`, `lineIdxForOffset`) per plan step 2, but every cell endpoint is still constructed as `{ blockId, offset }`: single click (text-editor.ts:1589), shift+click in cell (1578), and the cell drag focus via `resolveOffsetInCellAtXY` (1831-1840). So for a click at the start of a wrapped line inside a table cell the endpoint carries no affinity and the branch keeps its pre-existing hard-coded forward/backward defaults — behaviourally identical to before the change. The issue (#66, docs/tasks/active/20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md) does not list tables as out of scope (only double/triple click and the caret default are), so the fix is partial for the table surface while its plumbing cost is paid.

samples.summary: The updated design doc's Non-Goals now contradict its own body: it still lists "Redesigning `DocPosition` throughout `packages/docs`" and "Changing the visual caret rendering behavior" while the change extends `DocPosition` and changes selection-rect rendering defaults.
samples.evidence: Non-Goals at lines 59-60 are unchanged, but the new Proposal Details text at lines 76-94 adds `lineAffinity` to `DocPosition` and describes a new default (`start` reads forward) that changes painted geometry. Design-doc discipline expects the Non-Goals / Goals of the canonical subsystem doc to be reconciled when the scope widens, rather than leaving a doc that forbids in one section what it specifies in another. (Folding into this doc rather than creating a parallel file is the right call — only the Non-Goals need updating.)

samples.summary: `activeCursorPos.lineAffinity` is added to the wire type and published, but nothing consumes it — peer caret rendering hard-codes `'backward'`, so a peer's caret and their highlight can now sit a visual line apart.
samples.evidence: The new field is documented as "typing it keeps the wire shape honest" (users.ts:24-27) and docs/design/docs/docs-presence.md:189-197 admits peer caret rendering still hard-codes backward (editor.ts:1563) and calls honouring it a follow-up. Publishing a presence field with no reader, while the sibling selection field is honoured, introduces an internally inconsistent peer rendering state for no current benefit; either wire it through to the peer caret or leave it off the presence payload until the follow-up lands.

samples.summary: The pre-existing `DocPosition & { lineAffinity: 'forward' | 'backward' }` intersection types are now redundant with the field on `DocPosition` itself and were not consolidated.
samples.evidence: `find-position-at-pixel.ts:18` and `text-editor.ts:4312`, `4336`, `4441` all declare the hit-test return as `DocPosition & { lineAffinity: ... }`, a pattern that existed precisely because `DocPosition` lacked the field. Now that `DocPosition` carries it (model/types.ts:213) these intersections duplicate the declaration; collapsing them to a `required` variant (or leaving one helper type) would keep a single definition of the affinity contract.

verdict.reason: Every claimed fact checks out. selection.ts:260 does default an affinity-less START to 'forward' inside buildRects, the shared body of computeSelectionRects (selection.ts:547). That helper is used by non-selection consumers that pass ranges with no lineAffinity: peer selections (editor.ts:1620), search highlights (editor.ts:1640-1649), comment markers (editor.ts:1659-1665), spell squiggles (editor.ts:1676-1685, matching docs-spell-check.md:162), find scroll-into-view (editor.ts:3129-3135) and text-box-editor.ts:560, so the default flip changes their wrap-boundary geometry too. The change's own task file records this as a deliberate deviation from the issue's "keep the backward default" wording (20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md:18-26, 60-67) and justifies it only for user selections; docs-local-caret-anchoring.md:83-87 likewise frames the new default purely as selection-highlight behavior, with no analysis of the other consumers. No caller-side guard normalizes affinity before these call sites, the code is present as described, and an unmet stated acceptance criterion plus unanalysed scope widening is squarely within the design-fit lane, so none of not-present / already-guarded / out-of-scope applies.

After this change some call sites put the affinity on the position too (text-editor.ts:1521-1525, editor.ts restoreLocalCursor) while the keyboard paths do not: `handleHome` calls `this.cursor.moveTo(newPos, 'forward')` with `newPos` carrying no `lineAffinity` (text-editor.ts:2818), and `moveHorizontal`/vertical do the same at text-editor.ts:2780/2795 (the movers at text-editor.ts:3887-3999 build fresh `{blockId, offset}` objects). verdict.reason: Every element of the presence claim checks out in the tree. `Cursor.moveTo` writes `position` and `lineAffinity` as two unsynchronised fields (cursor.ts:28-32). The click path additionally stamps the affinity onto the position (text-editor.ts:1517-1525) and `restoreLocalCursor` has to pass the same value twice, once in the position literal and once as the moveTo argument (editor.ts:3599-3608) — the redundancy described. The keyboard paths do not: `handleHome` calls `moveTo(newPos, 'forward')` where `newPos` comes from `getVisualLineStart`, which returns a bare `{blockId, offset}` (text-editor.ts:2805/2818, 4061-4064), and `moveHorizontal` does the same (text-editor.ts:2780/2795) — the affinity is attached only to the selection focus, never to the caret position. Presence/anchoring reads `cursor.position` (editor.ts:1160, 2069 -> docs-view.tsx:394-407 -> yorkie-doc-store.ts:2999), so a Home/arrow caret publishes no affinity and `restoreLocalCursor` re-defaults it to 'backward', which is precisely the failure the new comment at editor.ts:3595-3598 says it prevents. No guard elsewhere fills in the affinity on the stored position. I weighed `out-of-scope` (propagation gap could read as correctness-lens), but the finding's substance is duplicated state / wrong abstraction for state this change introduced (DocPosition.lineAffinity in model/types.ts:200-213 next to the pre-existing Cursor.lineAffinity), which is within the design-fit lane — not a clean named refutation.

finding.summary: Table-cell selection endpoints never get a `lineAffinity`, so the cell-internal plumbing added to `buildRects` is unreachable and the reported wrap-boundary bug persists inside cells.
finding.evidence: The diff threads `startAffinity`/`endAffinity` into the cell-internal branch (`resolvePositionPixel`, `lineIdxForOffset`) per plan step 2, but every cell endpoint is still constructed as `{ blockId, offset }`: single click (text-editor.ts:1589), shift+click in cell (1578), and the cell drag focus via `resolveOffsetInCellAtXY` (1831-1840). So for a click at the start of a wrapped line inside a table cell the endpoint carries no affinity and the branch keeps its pre-existing hard-coded forward/backward defaults — behaviourally identical to before the change. The issue (#66, docs/tasks/active/20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md) does not list tables as out of scope (only double/triple click and the caret default are), so the fix is partial for the table surface while its plumbing cost is paid.

verdict.reason: Verified in the tree: every body table-cell selection endpoint is built without affinity — single click (text-editor.ts:1588-1593), shift+click (1577-1579), and same-cell drag focus (1842-1845, which overwrites the affinity-carrying pos from 1795-1799); the helpers resolveOffsetInCell/resolveOffsetInCellAtXY (4623, 4634) return only {blockId, offset}. Consumers exist (selection.ts:260-269 and lineIdxForOffset 337-366 feeding resolvePositionPixel), and local rects come only from Selection.getSelectionRects / computeSelectionRects (editor.ts:1544, selection.ts:547-564), which pass stored endpoints through unchanged, so the cell branch always sees the fallbacks 'forward'/'backward' that it already hard-coded. I searched wide for a counterexample and found only inert ones: shift+Home (text-editor.ts:2811-2814) can attach 'forward' to a cell block (cell-aware getVisualLineRange at 4020-4049) but that endpoint always normalizes to start, whose default is already 'forward'; and header/footer cells do carry affinity (resolveHFCellOffset 4513 -> 1521-1526, 1773-1777) but HF highlights go through computeHFSelectionRects/computeHFTableCellSelectionRects (editor.ts:798-817, 566-606), which ignore lineAffinity entirely — a different code path from buildRects. Shift+arrow inside a cell returns early (2459-2751) without affinity. So the table surface of the fix is unimplemented while its plumbing cost is paid, and tables are not listed under the todo's Out of scope (docs/tasks/active/20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md:60-67) — a major design-fit/spec-conformance gap.

finding.summary: docs-presence.md contradicts the code this same delta ships: the `DocsPresence` snippet still types `activeCursorPos` as `{ blockId, offset }`, and the §4 prose added in this delta asserts "`activeCursorPos` is not typed for the field" — but the delta adds `lineAffinity?: 'forward' | 'backward'` to `activeCursorPos` in `packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:25`. The canonical presence design doc is the wire-shape record for Docs presence (CONTRIBUTING requires the data-model change be folded into the canonical subsystem doc), so it must show the field on the caret payload too, or the field should not be added. As written, the doc will mislead the next reader about what the caret presence payload carries.
finding.evidence: docs-presence.md snippet: `activeCursorPos?: { blockId: string; offset: number; }` and prose "The peer *caret* still resolves `'backward'`: `activeCursorPos` is not typed for the field" vs users.ts adding `lineAffinity?: 'forward' | 'backward'` to activeCursorPos.

verdict.reason: Both pieces of quoted evidence are absent from the repository. (1) The `DocsPresence` snippet in the canonical doc does type the field: docs/design/docs/docs-presence.md:88-92 declares `activeCursorPos?: { blockId; offset; lineAffinity?: 'forward' | 'backward' }`, exactly matching packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:21-28. So the data-model change IS folded into the canonical subsystem doc as CONTRIBUTING requires. (2) The prose the finding quotes ("`activeCursorPos` is not typed for the field") does not exist. docs-presence.md:191-197 states the inverse — "the field rides along on `activeCursorPos`, but peer caret rendering hard-codes the backward reading (`editor.ts:1563`)" — and that is a correct description of the code: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1563 passes a literal 'backward'. The doc distinguishes wire shape (field present) from rendering behavior (affinity ignored, follow-up noted), which is consistent, not contradictory. The only affinity-free rendering of activeCursorPos is the informal ASCII flow diagram at line 278, which is not a type declaration and is not what the finding cites. There is no doc/code mismatch to block on.
